title: Spatial information and reproducible water science
blurb: A route through Ilya Zaslavsky’s interests in spatial integration and scientific infrastructure, using hydrologic information systems as the worked example.

person.name: Ilya Zaslavsky
person.affiliation: San Diego Supercomputer Center, UC San Diego
person.expertise: Spatial information systems, spatiotemporal integration, and distributed scientific data infrastructure

sources.title: SDSC spatial data science profile and teaching

papers.title: A relational model for environmental and water resources data

notes.takeaway: Store each observation with its location, variable, units, method, and provenance in a relational model.
notes.why: A shared schema makes cross-investigator comparisons possible without discarding measurement context.

papers.title: HydroDesktop: Web services-based software for hydrologic data discovery, download, visualization, and analysis

notes.takeaway: HydroDesktop combines discovery, download, visualization, and analysis across CUAHSI web services.
notes.why: A common client makes a distributed network usable to researchers.

papers.title: Observations Data Model 2: A community information model for spatially discrete Earth observations

notes.takeaway: ODM2 extends observation modeling to accommodate both sensors and specimens across scientific domains.
notes.why: Interoperability requires agreement about what observations mean, as well as how they are encoded.

papers.title: HydroShare: Sharing Diverse Environmental Data Types and Models as Social Objects with Application to the Hydrology Domain

notes.takeaway: HydroShare treats datasets and models as objects people can annotate, publish, and collaborate around.
notes.why: Scientific sharing includes unfinished work and conversation alongside formal publication.

papers.title: Map based discovery of hydrologic data in the HydroShare collaboration environment

notes.takeaway: Map-based discovery must balance spatial use cases, browser performance, and resources without geographic meaning.
notes.why: A bounding box is only one part of a scientific discovery interface.

papers.title: Collaborative sharing of multidimensional space-time data in a next generation hydrologic information system

notes.takeaway: NetCDF-based resources combine multidimensional space-time data with harvested metadata and access services.
notes.why: Gridded environmental data need structures beyond point time series.

papers.title: HydroDS: Data services in support of physically based, distributed hydrological models

notes.takeaway: HydroDS exposes terrain, climate, soil, and canopy preparation through Python-accessible web services.
notes.why: Reproducibility begins in input preparation, before the simulation runs.

papers.title: Toward open and reproducible environmental modeling by integrating online data repositories, computational environments, and model Application Programming Interfaces

notes.takeaway: Connects a data repository, notebook compute environments, and a model API in a reproducible hydrologic workflow.
notes.why: An executable study needs coordinated storage, computation, and model control.

papers.title: Community Workflows to Advance Reproducibility in Hydrologic Modeling: Separating Model-Agnostic and Model-Specific Configuration Steps in Applications of Large-Domain Hydrologic Models

notes.takeaway: Separates common preprocessing from model-specific configuration in reproducible SUMMA and mizuRoute workflows.
notes.why: Shared preparation steps can become reusable community infrastructure.

papers.title: Building cyberinfrastructure for the reuse and reproducibility of complex hydrologic modeling studies

notes.takeaway: Combines HydroShare, notebooks, containers, large-data transfer, and HPC for continental modeling.
notes.why: The same provenance problem persists as experiments outgrow a laptop.

papers.title: An extensible schema for capturing environmental model metadata: Implementation in the HydroShare online data repository

notes.takeaway: Introduces an extensible schema describing particular model applications while retaining a standard core.
notes.why: Comparing model instances requires both common fields and model-specific detail.

papers.title: HydroShare retrospective: Science and technology advances of a comprehensive data and model publication environment for the water science domain

notes.takeaway: Reviews a decade of HydroShare architecture, operation, usage, and research contributions.
notes.why: Long-term operation provides a test of infrastructure beyond an initial demonstration.

sections.label: Foundations: describing an observation
sections.summary: A value becomes usable evidence when its time, place, units, method, and history travel with it. Relational observation models and service clients made these descriptions consistent across independent data providers.
questions: Which context must remain attached to every measurement?

sections.label: Progression: from files to shared research objects
sections.summary: Repositories widened from point observations to models and multidimensional data. Collaborative annotation and spatial discovery brought scientists' workflows into the design of environmental information systems.
questions: How should a map represent data collected at different scales?

sections.label: Progression: making an analysis repeatable
sections.summary: Access services, data preparation, notebooks, and model APIs join the repository to the experiment. The challenge moves from finding a dataset to recording how it became the input to a particular simulation.
questions: What must be preserved to rerun a study without its original author?

sections.label: Frontier: reproducibility across systems and scales
sections.summary: Large models require coordinated computing, transfer, and metadata systems. Extensible descriptions and long-running repository experience expose the maintenance needed to keep research reusable.
questions: How can reuse preserve both computation and scientific intent?
